By which I am referring to a person who is fat but has at least started along the path to improving themselves.

Whether it's an old friend who let themselves go, or a new acquaintance who falls into the "small-fat" category but wants to lose weight.

Is it worth taking their hand and leading them along the path to becoming a normal-sized human? Going to the gym with them, hikes, cooking and eating better together, etc.

Does anyone have experience with doing this and can shed some light on the challenges or risks involved? I want to become fitter and thinner myself - does having another person (who's progress would frankly be much more obvious) help or hinder me? Is there a point at which I should give up on them if they aren't making progress?

I might get some vitriol for this sort of thought, I know the fat-hate runs deep but my personal hatred is a much more passive, brooding hate than most, so I don't very much care. Just looking to see if anyone else has done this sort of thing - turning an asteroid into a human - and what the end results were like.

I'm sure there are a few people who can help others find their own path without any problems, but before you choose to help someone you need to ensure that they will not drag you down or prevent you from reaching your own person goals.

If this person is a friend and they go back to their old ways after you have tried to help them, you could very easily lose a friend.

When it comes down to it, it is your body, your goals, your journey, and your life. You do you and if you happen to find a buddy along the way, great! But they have to want it enough to stay on track.

Many people stick with diet and exercise for a little while and then something happens, they get triggered, and backslide undoing months of progress in a short period of time.

I have tried to help people get to a healthy weight in the past and after a period of success they started cheating and simply have too many excuses for why they can't have some self control. It isn't difficult! Count calories and don't indulge beyond whatever they set to be their limit. Every one of them has failed.

Give it a try if you want to, but don't be surprised when the excuses start and the pounds are regained.

It is a Sisyphean task to keep rolling with boulders.
I hate fat people. But that doesn't stop me from helping them. If they return to a normal human size I see it as a win - one less fatty in this world.
Sometimes I think the only way a fat person will loose weight is with self hate. I don't think any amount of help can help someone who doesn't hate themselves.

Support them, encourage, but do not take over. If they ask, "wanna go the gym?" then go. NEVER say to them, "Hey, man, get off your ass, let's go to the gym!" You are setting yourself up for 1) Failure. 2) mental letdown, as the fat will mostly rely on you to do everything for them. 3) It's not your responsibility to be their coach/trainer/manager/life partner. 4) Failure.
